name: Aristotelis Mistakidis
current_role: Private investor; controlling shareholder of Aegean Baltic Bank and majority owner of PAOK BC (via Alpha Sports Group); ex-head of copper at Glencore
profile: Greek-British 'Telis' Mistakidis spent ~25 years at Marc Rich & Co./Glencore after six years trading metals at Cargill, rising to run Glencore's global copper business until 2018; the 2011 IPO made him a billionaire. He now invests in Greek banking (Piraeus, Aegean Baltic Bank), shipping (Union Maritime), real estate and sport.
interesting_fact: In November 2025 he became majority owner of Thessaloniki basketball club PAOK BC, and in 2026 the club announced a new privately operated training centre in Pylaia with two indoor courts.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in Rome, where his father, a marine biologist, worked for the United Nations; he told Kathimerini in 2011 that Greek was always spoken at home while he grew up abroad.
notes: Very private; no personal office contact published. Plausible routes: PAOK BC club press office or Aegean Baltic Bank corporate communications. Forbes bio notes a 2018 Canadian regulatory ban—avoid in outreach. Energy/commodities angle (copper, zinc) fits the podcast.

name: Allison McCain
current_role: Chairman, McCain Foods Ltd. (chair since 2004; no 2025-26 source found confirming he still holds the title)
profile: Allison D. McCain, nephew of McCain Foods co-founders Harrison and Wallace McCain, joined the Florenceville, N.B. frozen-potato giant in 1975 as an engineer, ran production in Australia and the UK, became deputy chairman in 1999 and chairman in 2004. His wealth is his family stake in privately held McCain Foods.
interesting_fact: As chair of UNB's 'Forging our Futures' campaign from 2003, he helped raise $107 million, then a record for Atlantic Canada; he later served as UNB's chancellor (named 2013) and chaired the Beaverbrook Art Gallery board.
deep_cut_fact: An electrical engineering graduate of UNB (1972), he worked at the New Brunswick Telephone Company before taking an engineering job at McCain's Florenceville plant in 1975 — the first of the family's next generation to join the firm.
notes: Low public profile; no personal accounts found. No death reports found (born c.1949). Best route is McCain Foods corporate communications. Only listed by Hurun 2014-2016.

name: Spiro Latsis
current_role: Head of the Latsis family group; chairman of EFG Bank European Financial Group; president of the John S. Latsis Public Benefit Foundation's supervisory board
profile: Spiros J. Latsis (b. 1946) is the son of Greek shipping-and-oil tycoon John S. Latsis (d. 2003) and has led the family's Latsis Group since then. Holdings include EFG International (Swiss private banking), Lamda Development (Athens real estate), a stake in Helleniq Energy and the TALOS shipyard. He also funds the Latsis foundations in Athens and Geneva.
interesting_fact: He holds three LSE degrees: a BSc in economics (1968), an MSc in logic and scientific method (1970) and a PhD in philosophy (1974). He is also a trustee of the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton.
deep_cut_fact: His PhD in philosophy at LSE was supervised by the famous philosopher of science Imre Lakatos, and he worked in the philosophy of economics before turning to the family business.
notes: Very private. The input Forbes bio appears to mix up names ('John and Margarita'); verify before quoting it. The foundation site warns about fraudulent emails that impersonate it. His Geneva family office (SETE SA) was named in a 2024 Swiss probe; per SETE he was not charged. Avoid this in outreach.

name: Miriam Baumann-Blocher
current_role: Owner and CEO, Läckerli Huus AG (Basel confectioner); shareholder in Ems-Chemie
profile: A food engineer (ETH Zurich) and daughter of Swiss politician and Ems-Chemie owner Christoph Blocher, she received an Ems-Chemie stake in 2004 when her father joined the Federal Council. She later sold most of it to her sisters. In 2007 she bought Basel's Läckerli Huus (founded 1904) and still runs it, with production consolidated in Frenkendorf.
interesting_fact: She tells Swissinfo that Läckerli Huus products contain no hidden sugar and that its Läckerli are sweetened mainly with honey. About 10% of sales come from outside Switzerland, mostly Germany and Japan.
deep_cut_fact: At 32, while researching companies to work for, she wrote to Läckerli Huus owner Mr. Klein. When he offered her the CEO job, she replied she would take it only if she owned the company, and he sold it to her. Her grandmother had given her Basel Läckerli every Christmas.
notes: Gives interviews about Läckerli Huus as an entrepreneur (Swissinfo, BaslerIN, Promarca). Best route is via Läckerli Huus. Keep the angle on entrepreneurship, not family politics.

name: Howard Butt III
current_role: CEO and board member, H-E-B (since 2021); board member, H.E. Butt Foundation
profile: Great-grandson of H-E-B founder Florence Butt and nephew of chairman Charles Butt, Howard Butt III succeeded his uncle as CEO of the family-owned Texas grocer in 2021. H-E-B has 455 stores in Texas and Mexico, about 160,000 employees and roughly $50 billion in sales. In 2025 he picked COO Roxanne Orsak as the company's first female president, starting in 2026.
interesting_fact: H-E-B gives 5% of pretax profits to charity each year. The company was started in 1905 by his great-grandmother Florence Butt.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming CEO he ran H-E-B's Mexico division (as of 2016). His father, Howard E. Butt Jr., co-created the Laity Lodge retreat center in the Texas Hill Country in 1961.
notes: Keeps a low media profile. The news@heb.com address came from a search snippet of an H-E-B page that loads by JavaScript, so I could not confirm it directly; check before use. H-E-B says media inquiries go to regional Public Affairs offices.

name: Wang Yi
current_role: Listed by Hurun alongside Liang Qin as co-holder of the Yangjie Technology fortune; exact role at the company unconfirmed
profile: Hurun lists Wang Yi with Liang Qin as owners of the Yangzhou Yangjie Electronic Technology (300373.SZ) fortune. Yangjie is a power-semiconductor maker that Liang Qin founded in 2000 and chairs. She is its sole disclosed actual controller, and its 2025 filings do not name Wang Yi, so his link to the company (likely family) is unverified.
interesting_fact: Yangjie Technology began in 2000 as a semiconductor brand-distribution business started by Liang Qin with about ten partners. It has since become a listed power-semiconductor (diodes, MOSFETs, SiC) manufacturer, a supplier to energy and EV-related markets.

public_contacts.value: zjb@21yangjie.com (Yangjie Technology, published in its 2024 ESG report; phone 0514-80889866)

notes: The name is ambiguous: 'Wang Yi' is also China's foreign minister, so do not confuse them. I could not confirm who this Wang Yi is. Yangjie's filings name only chairwoman Liang Qin as actual controller. Contact Yangjie via its published company email and confirm the relationship before any outreach.
